_readme: The goddess who brought you over (js/logic/goddess.js, docs/GODDESS.md). Numbers are in balance.json → goddess.
Placeholders: {goddess} her name, {sam}, {house}, {partner} (first name), {past} (your past life, lowercase), {lady} (a lady's first name), {n}, {names}, {cycle}, {skill}.
Any text field may be a list: one entry is picked at random.

rebirth: at every New Game+ before the binding. fast/steady/slow = how quickly you paid (weeks vs the plan). lovers/alone = lovers carried or none. jealous.low/mid/high by her jealousy. bound.low/mid/high = after the binding, by her divinity.

teases: her scenes before the binding, picked by evGoddess: story scenes (non-repeat) play in file order, each once, from minCycle on; maxCycle is only when they're due, a missed one stays available and makes her visit more often (balance.json → goddess.events.catchUp). Repeat scenes are filler, gated by minCycle-maxCycle, and only show once every unlocked story scene has been seen. Fields: id, title, text, choices [{label, res, love, jealousy, energy (yours), reveal}], minCycle, maxCycle, form ('disguise' = random non-true form, 'true' = her own form, or a form key), repeat (filler, may recur, never marked seen), unknown (only before you have worked it out), needKnows (only after), reveal (taking the event, or a choice with reveal, sets g.knows), image {comp, setting, sam, pov} (comp describes pose/scene only: the code adds her look). Placeholders: {alias} the name she gives in this form, {form} e.g. 'a fox-eared girl', {race}, {goddess} (only when you know / true form). Phases: stranger (cycles 1-2, st_*), suspicion (2-3, su_*), reveal (3), game (3-5, gm_*, after the reveal) and true-form scenes (3-5, tr_* and inside/almost/question). She never lets you finish: that would bind her.
remarks.low/mid/high: short jealous remarks (by jealousy) as weekly events, from cycle `remarksFrom` (3) on; remarkChoices are their default answers.

binding: the first rebirth after a lady has lived a fully reincarnated life; she confesses it was never a whim. focus: her weekly guidance options (report lines; indulge has feminine/futa variants, chosen by her form setting). claim: what she does when jealousy wins. night: your action on her tab (image, open by divinity low/mid/high, then inside / outside / unhappy lists by how the night ended; {act} = the service label, lowercase). ending.stay/leave: full divinity again.

intro: cycle 1, before the Vane welcome. Her remarks about houses, partners and your past lives live with them: economy.json → houses[id].goddess, pasts[k].goddess {intro, again}; characters.json → partner.goddess {hand, comment}. Her lines with the ladies are services.json → pair.fem/futa; on nights with you she uses the usual private-time lines (flavor.json → private_act).
neglect: report lines when you stay away (balance.json → goddess.neglect).

look: what never changes, so she's always recognizable: hairStyle, hair, eyes, skin, signature, outfit. forms[key]: one per race and beastkin sub (race, sub, build, body; label for the tab; alias = the name she gives when disguised; desc = how you first see her). trueForm = her own form (story scenes, rebirths). Each form has its own image id (npc_goddess_<key>), so pictures are saved per form.

distract: what happens when a disguise tease turns into her 'distracting' you (goddess.js evGoddessDistract, a second event page with a samact:<service> picture at the tease's setting). lead[phase] (stranger/suspicion/reveal/game) leads in; acts[service] is what she does (falls back to flavor.json private_act); dry[tier] is how she leaves you (1 = kisses: just wanting more; 2-3 = high and dry); button[tier] is the button before the ending. Teases and their choices may set lead / dry / act (service id or list) / distract (true/false) to override. Expanded teases: intro (her arrival, its own page, button introBtn) and wonder (your thoughts, shown with the choices); text is the fallback for old one-page scenes. A choice can only end in a distraction if it has resIn (what happens right before, she hasn't vanished yet; res stays the ending without one) or distract: true; then the phase chance (balance.json → goddess.tease.chance) or the tease's distract decides.

tabBlurb: Goddess of crossings and kept flames, currently bound to a former {past}, glowing a little less than she used to and not entirely sorry about it.

intro.title: Before the truck stops ringing

image.comp: a radiant goddess with a glowing bronze skin and a small ember-flame at her shoulder, sitting in a dark void lit by hundreds of hanging paper lanterns, looking down with an amused smile, one hand extended
image.setting: an endless dark space full of floating paper lanterns

intro.open:
The horn is still ringing when the dark fills up with lanterns. Hundreds of them, hanging from nothing.

A woman sits among them as if on a swing, barefoot, a little ember-flame drifting lazily around her shoulder. Her skin glows from within like a lantern, gold markings brightening at her collarbones and hips as she looks you over, slowly, head to toe, like someone deciding what to unwrap first.

"{sam} Takahashi. Thirty-one years of being nice to people and nobody ever once being nice back on purpose." She tilts her head. "I'm {goddess}. I light the way across, for the ones I pick. I picked you. On a whim, mostly. Don't read into it." She smiles like a woman who is reading into it a great deal.
intro.close:
"There's a debt. There's always a debt, it keeps you honest. Pay it, and if you're still interesting, I'll bring you back and we'll do it again." She trails one fingertip down your chest, leans close enough that her warmth fills the dark, and doesn't kiss you. "I'll be watching. Everything. Give me something worth watching."

The lanterns go out, one by one.

When you wake, the lanterns slip away like a dream, and by the time you're tying your shoes there is only a warm smell of candle smoke, and a faint feeling of having forgotten something that mattered.

rebirth.title: Again, {sam}?

image.comp: a radiant goddess with glowing bronze skin and a small ember-flame at her shoulder, lounging on a crescent of lantern-light, chin on her hand, smiling down, dress slipping off one shoulder
image.setting: an endless dark space full of floating paper lanterns

open:
The lanterns again. {goddess} is lying on her stomach across a crescent of light, chin in her hands, feet kicking idly, her dress slipping off one shoulder and no effort made to fix it.

"Debt paid. Look at you." She looks you over, unhurried. "Come here and let me see what the work did to you."

Darkness, then the warm smell of candle smoke. {goddess} is waiting, sitting on nothing, legs crossed, the little ember-flame circling her shoulder like a pet. "There you are. My favorite investment." She crooks a finger.

"Welcome back." {goddess} doesn't look up from the lantern she's turning in her hands. Inside it, very small, is the house you just left. "You did it again. I watched all of it. All of it, {sam}. You have no idea how much I enjoyed some of those nights."
fast: "That was quick. Show-off." She sounds pleased anyway. "I do like a man who gets the job done."
"Paid early. Marguerite nearly smiled, did you see? I had money on it. Now you owe me a kiss."
steady: "Right on schedule. Reliable. It's a good look on you." Her eyes drift down and back up. "Mostly."
"Not fast, not slow. You're very consistent, {sam}. I like a man with stamina."
slow: "That went right down to the wire. I had to watch through my fingers." She doesn't say which fingers she was using.
"You cut that close. Do you know how boring the afterlife paperwork is? Don't make me do it. I'd rather be doing you." She doesn't even pretend to have misspoken.
lovers: "And you're taking {names} with you." A pause that lasts slightly too long. "Of course you are. I hope they appreciate what I've been doing to keep you in such good shape."
"{names}. Again." She counts on her fingers and stops before she runs out. "Sweet. Do tell me everything later."
alone: "Nobody coming along this time? Hm." She looks like she wants to be disappointed for you and can't quite manage it. "More of you for me, then."

low: "Go on, then. Have fun. Tell me about it after."
"Enjoy yourself." A smile. "I will be, vicariously."
mid: "There are a lot of them now, {sam}." She says it lightly. She's looking at the lanterns, not at you.
"You know they don't remember me? Only you do. I find that very fair. Mostly."
high: She catches your chin before you go and holds it, thumb against your lip. "Every life, more of them. I brought you here. Remember that."
"I counted them. I didn't mean to. I count everything I'm not allowed to have." Her hand slides down your chest, and lingers.

close:
She kisses two fingers and presses them to your forehead, then, after a thought, to your mouth. The lanterns go out.

When you wake, the lanterns are already fading like a dream, and you can't quite remember whose face was looking down at you.
"Off you go." She flicks your nose, then smooths a hand down your front like she's checking the goods. The dark folds up like paper. The dream is going already; by morning it'll be gone.
"Don't keep me waiting." She almost sounds like she means something by it. Then the lanterns go out. You wake with the taste of candle smoke and nothing else.

low: This time there are no lanterns. {goddess} is just there when you wake, warm against your side, mortal-tired, one leg thrown over yours. "Again," she mumbles into your neck. "I'm coming too. Obviously."
mid: {goddess} wakes you by pressing close, glowing brighter than last time, the little ember-flame bobbing over her shoulder. "Another life. I'm getting some of it back, you know. Mostly thanks to you. Don't let it go to your head." She kisses you to make sure it does.
high: {goddess} is already up, glowing faintly, watching you sleep with her chin on her hand. "Nearly whole again," she says when you open your eyes, and slides closer. She doesn't say what happens then.

knows: "You remember," {goddess} says, before you've finished opening your eyes. She's grinning, and a little teary, and doesn't bother to hide either. "Each time you wake up you forget a bit less. Good. I like being known." She pulls you close by the collar. "Now come here, and let me remind you what you've been missing."

"Hello, {sam}. Don't say it, I know: you knew it was me the whole time." {goddess} is lounging across the dark, eyes half-lidded, thoroughly smug. "You're getting good at this. Go on. Go and pay your debt, and I'll find a new face to tease you with." She trails a fingertip down your chest and stops, exactly where she always stops.

teases.title: A stranger at the bar

image.comp: a girl sitting very close to a man at a bar counter, her hand on his thigh, leaning in to whisper in his ear, teasing smile
image.setting: the bar of a lantern-lit pleasure house at night

teases.text:
The girl at the end of the bar isn't a guest and isn't staff, and she's been watching you over the rim of her glass for ten minutes. {form}, very long black hair, gold at the tips, eyes that catch the lamplight a little too well.

"{alias}," she says, when you finally go over, as if you'd asked. "You're the owner. You look like you haven't sat down since the morning." She hooks a foot around your stool and pulls it closer. "Sit. Let someone look after you for once."

She does, for an hour: a hand on your knee, a thumb along your jaw, a laugh against your ear. Then you look down at your drink, and when you look up again the stool is empty and the glass is still warm.

choices.label: "Have we met?"
choices.resIn: "Mm. Have we?" She tilts her head, considering you, and something in her eyes looks almost pleased that you asked.
choices.res: "Not yet," she says, and taps your nose. You look down at your drink for one heartbeat, and when you look up the stool is empty and her glass is still warm. You check the hall, the stairs, the street. Nobody.

choices.label: Enjoy it while it lasts
choices.resIn: You stop trying to work her out and let the noise of the bar fade. She notices, and her smile turns slow and very warm.
choices.res: You let her talk, and let her hand wander, and for an hour this world feels kind. Then you blink, and she's gone, and the stool beside you is empty. A lucky night, wasted. You tell yourself these things happen. In this world, apparently, they do.

teases.intro:
The bar is loud tonight, which is good for business and bad for your head. You've been on your feet since dawn: ledgers, a broken shutter, a client who wanted a refund for reasons he declined to explain.

The girl at the end of the counter isn't a guest and isn't staff. She's been there for ten minutes with one untouched glass, watching you over the rim of it. {form}, with very long black hair that turns to gold at the tips, and eyes that catch the lamplight a little too well.

When you finally go over to ask if she needs anything, she answers before you can. "{alias}." As if you'd asked. "You're the owner. You look like you haven't sat down since this morning." She hooks a foot around the stool beside her and drags it closer. "Sit. Let someone look after you for once."
teases.wonder:
You sit. You aren't sure why. She talks about nothing (the weather, the music, the terrible painting over the door) and her hand settles on your knee as if it's always lived there.

You try to place her. Not one of your ladies. Not a client's companion; she came alone. Not anyone from the street, either: you would remember hair like that, the way the gold at the ends seems to glow a little in the dark corners of the room. There's something familiar about her laugh, though, like a song you heard once in a dream and can't quite hum.

Her thumb traces your jaw. "You're thinking very hard," {alias} says. "About me?"

teases.title: A visitor in the night

image.comp: a girl sitting on the edge of a man's bed at night leaning in for a kiss, her hand under the blanket, candle-light

teases.text:
You wake because the room is warm. Someone is sitting on the edge of your bed: {form}, black hair spilling over her shoulders, gold tips glowing faintly in the dark.

"Shh. I'm {alias}. You didn't hear me come in." She leans down and kisses you, slow and very thorough, one hand sliding under the blanket to rest on your stomach. You're too startled to do anything but kiss back. Her hand drifts lower. Lower. And the bed is empty, the door is shut and locked, and the room is cold.

choices.label: Kiss her back
choices.res: You catch the last of it before she's gone, and lie awake for an hour, aching. Somewhere far off, someone laughs, pleased.
choices.resIn: You open your mouth to say something, anything, and she catches the words before they leave, with a kiss that is slow and unhurried and entirely sure of itself. The blanket slides lower.

choices.label: "Who are you?"
choices.res: "Someone who likes you," says the dark, amused, from nowhere. "Goodnight, {sam}."
choices.resIn: "Who are you?" She seems to find the question adorable. "Someone who couldn't sleep," she murmurs, and her mouth finds yours before you can ask a second one, her hand wandering down under the blanket.

teases.intro:
The house has gone quiet the way it only does after the last guest is out and the last lantern is trimmed. You've been asleep for an hour, face down, one arm hanging off the mattress, dreaming about spreadsheets.

What wakes you is the warmth. Not the blanket kind: the kind that has a weight to it, sitting on the edge of the bed and making the mattress dip. Candle smoke, faint and sweet, as if someone had just walked in from a room full of them.

{form} is sitting there in the dark, black hair spilling over her shoulders so long it pools on the sheets, the tips glowing a soft gold. Her eyes are the color of lamplight. "Shh," she says, before you can get a word out. "I'm {alias}. You didn't hear me come in."
teases.wonder:
You're almost sure this is a dream. The door was locked; you locked it yourself. The window is two floors up. And yet there is a very solid, very warm person on your bed, and her hand is resting on your stomach through the blanket as if she'd been invited.

You don't know her. You're certain you don't know her. So why does the shape of her smile feel like a word on the tip of your tongue? Why does the smoke in the air remind you of somewhere high and golden, with paper lanterns swaying in a warm wind?

She leans closer, her hair sliding across your chest like cool silk, and waits to see what you'll do with the moment.

teases.title: Between the shelves

image.comp: a girl pressing a man back against shelves in a dim storeroom, kissing his neck, her hand at his belt

teases.text:
You're fetching linens from the storeroom when the door clicks shut behind you. {alias}, {form}, is leaning against it with her arms behind her back, looking you over like a shopkeeper's window.

"You work too hard." She pushes you back against the shelves and presses against you, warm and close, her mouth at your throat, her hand finding your belt. "Let me help."

You're gasping, nearly there, when a knock sounds outside. "Sam? Are you in there?" You turn your head. When you turn back, the storeroom is empty, and the door is open a crack.

choices.label: Follow her out
choices.res: The hall is empty. A single gold hair is caught on your collar. You pick it off and stare at it for a while.
choices.resIn: "Wait, that door was locked from the inside." She smiles, as though you've said something sweet, and slides closer, deaf to the logistics.

choices.label: Stay and collect yourself
choices.res: It takes a while. The blushing lasts longer. A strange girl, a locked door and a convenient knock. This place is wild.
choices.resIn: You don't say no. You don't say anything, and {alias} takes the silence as the yes it is, her fingers curling in the front of your shirt.

teases.intro:
The linen storeroom is the one place in the house that is always quiet, which is why you go there when you need to think. Today you need towels, and three minutes where nobody asks you anything.

You have an armful of folded sheets when the door clicks shut behind you. You turn. {form} is leaning against it with her hands behind her back, in the dusty gold light from the one high window, looking you over the way a person looks over a shop display they've already decided to buy.

Her hair is black and ridiculously long, the tips glowing like embers. Her skin is bronze, her eyes lamp-bright. "You work too hard," she says, as if you'd been talking all morning. "{alias}. Put those down."
teases.wonder:
You put them down. You have no idea why; your hands just do it. Maybe because no one has looked at you like that in a very long time, or maybe because she smells of candle smoke and warm skin and your brain has stopped taking orders.

You've been through every face in this house. Staff, guests, suppliers, the woman who sells lamp oil on the corner. She isn't any of them. And yet when she steps off the door and comes toward you, unhurried, there's a feeling in your chest like recognizing a handwriting.

She lays a hand flat on your chest, pushing you gently back until the shelves meet your shoulders. "Well?" she says, tilting her head. "Do you want me to stop?"

teases.title: Hot water

image.comp: a girl sitting behind a man in a steaming bath, her arms around his chest, teasing smile, steam
image.setting: a steaming wooden bath at night, lanterns

teases.text:
The bath is already hot when you get in, and already occupied. {alias} settles in behind you, wraps both arms around your chest and hooks her chin over your shoulder. She's {form}, and there is nothing at all between her skin and your back.

"Breathe," she murmurs, hands wandering. They know exactly where they're going, and exactly when to stop. "That's all you get tonight."

You turn your head to answer and the water is just water, rippling gently around you, and the steam smells faintly of candle smoke.

choices.label: Lean back into her
choices.res: You lean into nothing, and the water holds you warm and still. You come out of it oddly rested, and extremely frustrated.
choices.resIn: You let your head fall back against her shoulder. "Breathe," she says, and her hands begin to travel.

choices.label: Turn around
choices.res: You turn around fast enough to splash. No one. A ripple of laughter lingers somewhere near the ceiling.
choices.resIn: You start to turn, and a hand on your cheek gently stops you. "Not yet. Eyes on the water, {sam}." And you find you don't mind obeying.

teases.intro:
The bathhouse at the back of the property is your one luxury, a deep tiled tub fed by a hot spring that somebody before you had the good sense to build over. You get in at the end of the longest day of the week with a groan that would embarrass you in front of staff.

The water is perfect. The steam is thick. For a full minute you just float there with your eyes closed, listening to the lanterns tick as they cool.

Then the water moves. Not much: a ripple behind you, a soft sound of someone settling. When you open your eyes, a pair of bronze arms slide around your chest from behind and a chin hooks over your shoulder. {form}, black hair floating around you both like ink in the water, gold at the ends. "Don't turn around," says {alias}, warm against your ear. "I'm shy."
teases.wonder:
She is clearly not shy. You know this the way you know the water is wet. But it's hard to argue with her when her hands are drifting over your shoulders, working out knots you didn't know you had.

Who gets into a bath with a man they've never met? Who knows exactly where you carry the tension, and exactly how hard to press? The steam smells of candle smoke, which is strange, because the bath lamps burn lamp oil. Strange, and faintly familiar, in the way of a smell from a childhood you never had.

Her lips brush the back of your neck. "You're thinking again," she says. "I can hear it. Do you want me to make it stop?"

teases.title: The long way home

image.comp: a girl pushing a man against an alley wall, kissing him, her thigh between his, her hand inside his shirt
image.setting: a lantern-lit back alley at dusk

teases.text:
You're walking back from the market when a hand takes your wrist and pulls you into an alley. {alias}, {form}, pushes you against the wall with a grin and kisses you until your knees go. Her thigh slips between yours; her fingers are inside your shirt.

"Do you always walk home alone?" she whispers. "Someone should do something about that." Her hand moves, and moves, and you're almost, almost, almost-

Then a cart rattles past the mouth of the alley, and when it's gone you're standing there alone, breathless, with your shirt untucked and the faint sense that you've been teased on purpose.

choices.label: Chase after her
choices.res: Nobody in the alley, nobody in the street. You walk home with your coat held in front of you.
choices.resIn: You try to say you have errands, and she kisses the word right out of your mouth. The parcels can wait.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.res: This world runs on strange luck. The kind that gets you kissed in an alley and then leaves you shaking. You're not sure whether that's good or bad luck.
choices.resIn: You laugh, a little helplessly, because what else do you do, and the sound seems to please her. "Good," she says. "Stay right there."

teases.intro:
The market has been a long, loud errand: oil, linen, a haggle over soap that you lost on principle. You're cutting through the narrow lane behind the dyers' street, arms full of parcels, when the light goes strange.

A hand closes on your wrist. A very warm hand, with firm fingers. Before you have time to protest, the parcels are on the cobbles and your back is against the cool brick of an alley wall, and {form} is smiling up at you from very close.

Her hair falls to her knees, black as a night sky and tipped with gold that shines faintly even in the shade. Her eyes are the color of lamplight on honey. "Do you always walk home alone?" she asks. "{alias}. Hello."
teases.wonder:
There is a cart rattling somewhere beyond the mouth of the alley. A man is shouting about fish. The world carries on at the edge of your hearing, and none of it seems to have anything to do with the woman who has you by the collar.

Having been in this world a short while and already been pickpocketed twice, you should be checking your purse. Instead you're trying to remember where you've seen that exact shade of gold. In a dream, perhaps. Or lanterns, lots of them, floating up into a warm dark.

Her knee shifts lightly against yours. "You haven't said a word," {alias} observes, delighted with herself. "Should I be worried?"

teases.title: A stranger sits down
teases.text: A girl sits down next to you, uninvited: {form}, with very long black hair and gold-tipped ends. "{alias}," she says, and holds out a hand you don't get to shake. She lays it on your thigh instead, and talks about nothing for ten minutes while her fingers draw slow patterns higher and higher. Then she excuses herself to 'fix her hair', and doesn't come back.

choices.label: Ask what she wants
choices.res: She laughs and drops the topic, her fingers sliding off your knee. Whoever she was, she's not there when you look again, only a cooling chair and a faint smell of smoke. You go back to work grinning like a fool.
choices.resIn: "What I want?" She seems to enjoy the question. "Hold still and I'll show you," she says, and leans in until all you can see are her eyes.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: You finish the tea, and after a while realize it is the only warm thing left at the table. You don't mention to anyone why your face is red.
choices.resIn: You say nothing, and she hums approvingly, her hand traveling slowly, and with great confidence, higher.

teases.intro:
It is a slow afternoon, and you've sat down at the corner table to let your tea go cold. You don't see her arrive. One moment the chair beside you is empty; the next, {form} is in it, as if she'd been there all along.

Very long black hair, gold at the tips. Eyes like lamplight. A trace of candle smoke. "{alias}," she says, and holds out a hand. When you reach for it she lays it on your thigh instead.
teases.wonder:
Again. The thought comes before the word does. You have no reason to think "again", because you've never met this girl. And yet something inside you shrugs and says: of course.

Her fingers are drawing slow patterns on your knee while she talks about nothing in particular. You should probably say something. You're just not sure what question to ask first.

teases.title: A wink in the crowd
teases.text: In the middle of a busy evening, {alias} is just there: {form}, hip against the counter beside you, slipping one hand into your pocket and out again with a coin you hadn't known you had. "Tip," she says. She tucks it into your collar, brushes her lips against your ear, and her hand lingers at your waist just a moment too long. By the time the crowd shifts she has gone.

choices.label: Ask her name again
choices.res: You turn to ask and the space beside you is just space. The coin is warm against your collarbone. It is also gold, and by morning it is gone.
choices.resIn: "{alias}," she repeats, amused, and her fingers find the hem of your shirt under the counter's edge. "Pay attention."

choices.label: Play along
choices.res: The crowd shifts, someone shouts for a refill, and when you look again she is gone. You spend the rest of the shift touching your collar.
choices.resIn: You pocket your embarrassment and lean into her. She smiles against your jaw, and the noise of the room seems to retreat a step.

teases.intro:
The evening rush is in full cry, glasses and laughter and a lute somewhere in the back, and you're wedged against the counter checking tabs. A hip bumps yours, unhurried, and {form} is simply there beside you.

Hair so long it nearly touches the floor, black with burning gold tips. Her skin is bronze, her eyes a bright lamp-gold. She holds up a coin between two fingers. "Found this in your pocket," says {alias}. "I thought you'd like it back."
teases.wonder:
You didn't know you had a coin in that pocket. You didn't know a stranger could reach into it so gracefully. You're not even sure when she crossed the room.

She tucks the coin into your collar and presses close, with the whole crowd packed around you and no one so much as glancing over. Her breath is warm against your ear, and the smell of candle smoke lingers like a hand on the back of your neck.

teases.title: Someone is watching
teases.text:
The back stairs are dim, and someone is waiting at the top of them: {form}, long black hair, gold tips, lit from within. {alias} takes the lapels of your coat and walks you backward into the wall, kissing you with a hunger you can feel in your spine. Her knee presses. Your breath breaks.

"Later," she promises, and slips out of your hands like smoke.

choices.label: Ask what she's doing
choices.res: "Later," she promises, and the shadows swallow her. The lamp has burned down by the time you think to move.
choices.resIn: "What does it look like?" She tugs you down by the collar and answers the question in her own way.

choices.label: Kiss her
choices.res: The stairs are empty, the lamp flickers, and you stay there for a long moment, one hand against the wall.
choices.resIn: You kiss her, because it seems like the only sensible answer, and feel her smile against your mouth.

teases.intro:
The back stairs are dim at this hour. You're on your way up with a lamp when you realize someone is waiting at the top, and not one of your people. {form}, tall in the half-light, her black hair so long it brushes the steps, the gold tips lit as if from within.

"Late," says {alias}, and she doesn't say it as a complaint. She takes your lapels. You let her.
teases.wonder:
The lamp is shaking a little in your hand. You haven't even noticed. You're too busy trying to pin down why this feels like a continuation of something and not a beginning.

She walks you backward until the wall meets your shoulder blades and presses close, warm and certain. Smoke and honey and a slow, steady heat. Whoever she is, she isn't in a hurry.

teases.title: The same hair

image.comp: a girl perched on the corner of a desk, crossing her legs, leaning in to run a finger along a man's tie, teasing smile

teases.text:
It's {alias} again: {form}, a different girl, with a different name and a different pair of ears. You're at the desk when she perches on the corner of it, crossing her legs slowly, and asks how your night is going.

You're looking at her hair. Very long. Black. Gold at the tips, glowing faintly. The last girl had the same. And the one before that.

"Something wrong?" She leans in, smiling, and runs a finger along your tie. "You're staring."

choices.label: "Have we met?"
choices.res: "Haven't we all?" She taps your nose and kisses you on the corner of the mouth, and the door clicks, and she is not there. The pattern is getting hard to ignore.
choices.resIn: "Have we met?" She doesn't flinch. Her smile only deepens, and she slides off the desk and into your lap as though that were the answer.

choices.label: Say nothing, but watch her eyes
choices.res: Gold. Glowing. Exactly the same gold. She notices you noticing, and her smile grows slow and pleased. She's gone before you can ask.
choices.resIn: You say nothing and watch her eyes, and she notices you noticing, and for a beat the smile goes very still. Then it softens, and she leans close enough to kiss.

teases.intro:
It is late, the ledgers are open, and you're three columns from the end of the month when the lamp on your desk dims, flares, and steadies. You don't look up. Habit by now. Something in you already knows what's coming.

The desk creaks. {alias} has settled on the corner of it, {form}, a different girl with a different name and a different pair of ears, crossing her legs slowly and asking how your night is going. She says it warmly. She says it as if she had every right.

You glance up, and then you can't look away. Very long black hair. Gold at the tips, glowing. It isn't that she looks like the last one. It's that nothing about her looks different at all.
teases.wonder:
The last girl had the same. And the one before that. You've been telling yourself it's a trend, some fashion in this world for dyed gold, or lantern-glow powder. But the eyes are the same lamp-gold too, and the warm bronze skin, and the faint sweetness of candle smoke clinging to her.

You're counting now. You didn't mean to start, but once you notice a pattern you can't un-notice it. Every one of them has appeared on a day when you'd been alone. Every one of them has vanished before you could get a straight answer.

She runs a finger lightly along your tie. "You're staring," she says, in a voice that is not quite hers and not quite someone else's. "Is something wrong?"

teases.title: Always the same
teases.text:
You've made a list. It's a short, embarrassing list: a fox, a cat, an elf, a dwarf. Each one a stranger, each with the same hair, the same eyes, the same warm bronze skin, and each one gone just before you-

You're staring at it when {alias} comes in, {form}, and reads it over your shoulder. "What's this?"

"A coincidence," you say, and she laughs, pressing herself against your back, her hands sliding around your waist. "Poor thing. You've been so frustrated."

choices.label: "You know exactly why."
choices.res: "Do I?" Her breath on your neck is hot enough to hurt. "Maybe I'm just a bad girl. Maybe you're just unlucky." She nips your ear. The door closes behind nobody.
choices.resIn: "You know exactly why." You feel her go quiet, very briefly, against your spine. Then her hands move again, as though it were all part of the plan.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: "Oh, I'd love to." She does, exactly until you're about to say something clever. Then you're alone with your list.
choices.resIn: "Stay. Please." She goes very soft at that. "Oh, I'd love to," she says, and turns your chair around so she can look at you properly.

teases.intro:
You've made a list. It's a short, embarrassing list, written on the back of an invoice with a pencil you keep sharpening: a fox, a cat, an elf, a dwarf. Four columns: hair, eyes, skin, smell. Every line says the same thing four times.

You're still staring at it when the door opens without a knock. {alias} walks in as if she lived here, {form}, and drifts around the desk. She reads the list over your shoulder, and you feel her chin settle on it, smoke and warmth against your neck.

"What's this?" she asks lightly. "Homework?"
teases.wonder:
"A coincidence," you say, and she laughs, a low, delighted sound. It is the same laugh. Of course it is. You just never noticed, because the ears were different.

Your pencil is shaking. Four girls, no, five now. All of them arrive with no warning and leave the same way. All of them stop, always, always, just before you can-

She's pressed up against your back now, hands sliding around your waist, her mouth near your ear. "Poor thing," {alias} murmurs. "You've been so frustrated. Tell me about it."

teases.title: Questions

image.comp: a girl in a man's lap in an armchair, his hands on her wrists, her face close to his, a finger against his lips, teasing

teases.text:
You're done being teased in silence. When {alias} appears, {form}, slipping into your lap with an easy smile, you catch her wrists.

"Who are you?"

"{alias}. I told you." She wriggles. Her hips do something distracting. "Ask a better question."

"Why do you always leave before-"

"Ah." She presses a finger to your lips. "Wrong question too. Try again in a few lives." She kisses you instead of answering, very thoroughly, and you do not notice the 'lives' until much later.

choices.label: "Who are you?"
choices.res: "{alias}," she says, "I told you." It's the lightest voice she's used so far, and it hides something. She slips out of your hands like water, laughing. "Ask me again in a few lives."
choices.resIn: "{alias}. I told you." She seems almost fond. "Ask a better question, {sam}." Her hips shift in your lap, a slow and very effective argument.

choices.label: "Why do you always leave?"
choices.res: "Ah." She presses a finger to your lips. "Try again in a few lives." Then she's gone, and you're alone with the word 'lives', turning it over.
choices.resIn: "Wrong question," she says gently, and lays a finger across your lips. "Let me give you a better one." Her other hand slides slowly down your chest.

teases.intro:
You've had enough of being teased in silence. You've been up for three days working on a plan, and the plan is simple: the next time one of them shows up, you are going to hold on.

You're at your desk, pretending to read, when {alias} slips in. {form} again, hair like a curtain of night with gold at the ends, hips swaying. She doesn't bother with a greeting. She crosses the room, drops lightly into your lap, and starts to loosen your collar.

You catch her wrists. Not hard. Just enough. Her eyebrows go up, interested, and she doesn't pull away.
teases.wonder:
Her pulse is quick under your thumbs. That's something: she has a pulse, she's warm, she's here. Not a ghost, not a dream, not a figment of overwork. You've been making excuses for weeks and this is the first time you've had the evidence in your hands.

You have a dozen questions lined up. Who are you. What are you. Why me. Why do you always go before it matters. The longer you look into those lamp-gold eyes, the more you think she already knows every one of them, and has the answers sitting ready.

She wriggles a little, and your thoughts scatter. "Ask," says {alias}, with a smile like a dare. "I'm listening."

teases.title: Smoke and candle
teases.text:
You can't stop thinking about the dream. Gold lanterns, hundreds of them. A woman, laughing. Every time you reach for the details, they slide away. But when {alias} comes through the door, {form}, and you smell candle smoke, you know exactly where you've smelled it before.

She tries to kiss you. You turn your head.

"What's wrong?" Her smile slips for a heartbeat. "You're being strange."

"You smell like lanterns," you say.

choices.label: Hold her wrists, gently
choices.res: "{sam}." Her voice is small. "Not yet." She presses her forehead against your chest for three long breaths. Then she's gone, and for the first time, you think she wanted to stay.
choices.resIn: You take her wrists, gently, and hold on. She stills at once, and you can feel her heart beating through your fingers, quick and shy. "{sam}," she says, much too softly.

choices.label: Pull her in and ask again
choices.res: "Don't." She kisses you to stop you, and it's a worse kiss, more frightened. She slips away. You are nearly sure now.
choices.resIn: You draw her in and ask again, quietly. Her breath catches. "Don't," she whispers, and presses her mouth to yours, as if to stop the question where it stands.

teases.intro:
You can't stop thinking about the dream. Gold lanterns, hundreds of them, rising against a violet sky. A woman laughing, somewhere just out of reach. Every time you reach for the details they slide away like fish. You've been absent-minded all day, losing track of conversations, staring at the flames in the hall.

That's why you catch the smell first. Candle smoke, warm and sweet, at your shoulder before the door has even finished opening. {alias} comes in, {form}, all long black hair and gold tips, and the dream rushes back so hard you have to put a hand on the wall.

She crosses to you, smiling, and leans in for a kiss. You turn your head, and her mouth lands on your cheek.
teases.wonder:
Lanterns. That's the thing you know now. The smell, the gold, the way the light follows her as if it belongs to her. It isn't hair dye and it isn't a trick. Whoever she is, she is the woman from the dream, and every single girl before her was her too.

You feel oddly calm. The questions you'd been rehearsing have fallen away, and what's left is a quiet certainty, and a name rising from somewhere under your ribs. Not yet. You can almost taste it.

"What's wrong?" {alias} asks, and her smile slips for a heartbeat. "You're being strange." You look at her, really look, at the eyes like flame behind glass. "You smell like lanterns," you say.

teases.title: Another one
teases.text: {alias}, {form}, is already sitting on the stairs when you come up, ankles crossed, glowing faintly. "You're late." She pulls you down beside her and kisses you, a warm lazy kiss, one hand tucked inside your shirt. "Didn't you miss me?" She's gone before you've finished deciding, leaving you with the gold hair on your sleeve and an uneasy thought.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." Your voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and you think you hear a laugh.
choices.resIn: "Whoever you are-" you begin, and she kisses the rest of it away, slow and lazy and warm, one hand slipping inside your shirt.

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: You hold a long black hair up to the lamp. Gold at the tip. Exactly like all the others.
choices.resIn: You smile and say nothing, which she plainly takes as encouragement. Her fingers play along your ribs.

teases.intro:
The upper landing is dark and smells of lamp oil, and coming up with a tray of clean glasses, you nearly walk into someone's crossed ankles. {alias} is sitting on the top stair, {form}, glowing faintly in the gloom, black hair coiled around her like a sleeping cat, gold at the tips. Her eyes catch the single lamp below and hold it.

"You're late," she says, as though you'd made plans. She pulls you down beside her by the sleeve, the glasses chiming in your hands, and tucks herself against your side with the unhurried comfort of someone who's done this before.
teases.wonder:
Different ears, different name, same everything. You don't even have to count anymore. The hair, the eyes, the faint candle sweetness in the air: a signature, more than a disguise.

She watches you work it out, a little smile tucked into the corner of her mouth, as if daring you to say it aloud. "Didn't you miss me?" she asks, and her hand finds its way inside your shirt.

teases.title: Her eyes, again
teases.text:
You find yourself watching a girl's eyes: {alias}, {form}, who has appeared, as they always do, in the middle of a quiet hour. Glowing gold. She catches you at it and her smile deepens. She walks you to the wall, slow, and you let her. "Looking for something?" she asks, and her hand slips into your waistband.

You don't get to answer.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." Your voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and you think you hear a laugh.
choices.resIn: You try to ask, and she answers by pulling you close, her hand slipping lower. "Not yet, {sam}," she says, and the name lands strangely.

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: Gold. Always the same gold. You are counting now.
choices.resIn: You smile and say nothing, watching her eyes. Hers narrow, pleased, and she crowds closer.

teases.intro:
It's a quiet hour, the house humming low, the kind of lull in which you usually restock shelves and think about nothing. Today you're thinking about gold. You're straightening a row of lamp oil tins when you feel it: that prickle at the back of the neck of being watched.

{alias} is leaning in the doorway, {form}, arms folded, a spill of black hair reaching past her hips and glowing at the ends. Her eyes are lamp-gold, warm and glowing and amused. She's caught you staring, you realize; you've been staring at nothing for a full minute, waiting for her. She strolls over, slow, and you let her walk you back against the wall.
teases.wonder:
Gold. Always the same gold, with the same slow glow at the edges, like a lamp seen through a windowpane. Five girls, six, and one pair of eyes. You've stopped telling yourself it's a coincidence. You've started wondering what, exactly, you are supposed to do with the knowledge.

Her hand settles at your waist. "Looking for something?" asks {alias}, quietly, and you get the strangest feeling that she wants you to answer honestly. That she would be pleased if you did.

teases.title: Different ears, same girl
teases.text: {alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the same everything else. She walks around you in a slow circle, trailing a hand across your shoulders. "What do you think? Do I suit it?" You think you're on to her. You think you're missing something, too. By the time you can say any of it, the chair beside you is empty.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." Your voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and you think you hear a laugh.
choices.resIn: "Whoever you are-" you begin, and a hand slides over your mouth. "Hush," she whispers. "Let's not spoil it."

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: You sit there for a minute, then go and check the mirror in the hall. Nothing in it but you.
choices.resIn: You smile, saying nothing, and she circles round to face you and settles in your lap, a thoughtful look in her lamp-gold eyes.

teases.intro:
{alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the same everything else. You find her in the middle of the sitting room, turning on one heel to model them, as though you'd asked. Soft ears, a swish of tail, and underneath it all the same long black hair, the same gold at the tips swinging as she moves.

She walks a slow circle around your chair, trailing a fingertip over your shoulders as she goes, and the smell of candle smoke follows her like a cloak. "What do you think?" she asks. "Do I suit it?"
teases.wonder:
You think you're on to her. You think you're missing something, too: some detail so obvious that it keeps hiding in plain sight. The ears are charming. The girl under them is the same girl you've been losing for weeks, and you're almost sure that if you ask the right question, in the right voice, she'll answer.

She stops behind you and rests her chin on top of your head. "You're quiet," says {alias}, warm and curious. "Dangerous. Out with it."

teases.title: Say my name

image.comp: a girl in a man's lap, arms around his neck, forehead to his, a startled and delighted look, candles flaring around them
image.setting: Sam's bedroom at night, every candle burning gold

teases.text:
She comes to you as {alias} tonight, {form}, with a smile that is a little too wide. She sits in your lap, loops her arms around your neck, and you let her. You let her all the way to the edge of the kiss.

Then you say, quietly, "{goddess}."

Everything stops. Her smile stays where it is; her eyes don't. The candles dip. You don't know where the name came from: a dream of paper lanterns, a woman swinging in the dark, a promise about a debt. It was just there on your tongue.

"...Well," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore. "That took you long enough."

choices.label: "You've been teasing me for years."
choices.res: "Lives," she corrects, and kisses you, laughing and furious and relieved, all at once. "You remembered. You actually remembered. Don't stop." She stays a good long while this time.
choices.resIn: Everything stops. Her smile stays where it is; her eyes don't. Then she kisses you, hard and fast, as if to catch the name before it escapes, and starts working at your collar.

choices.label: "Why the disguises?"
choices.res: "Because the game is more fun when you don't know the rules." She presses her forehead to yours. "And because I was afraid you'd say no, once you knew. Foolish of me." The glow around her brightens, a little shy.
choices.resIn: Her breath catches. For the first time, she doesn't have a quick answer. "Later," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore, and kisses you so you can't ask again.

teases.intro:
She comes to you as {alias} tonight, {form}, with a smile that is a little too wide. You're on the roof of the house, where you go when the noise gets to be too much, and the lanterns hang below you like a field of tiny gold stars.

She doesn't knock; there's nothing to knock on. She just steps out of the dark, trailing candle smoke, sits in your lap and loops her arms around your neck. Her hair falls over you both, black and endless, the tips glowing in the dark.

You let her. You let her all the way to the edge of the kiss.
teases.wonder:
The thing about the dream is that it isn't a dream. It's a memory. Gold lanterns, a swing hung from nothing, a woman laughing at you in the dark. A promise about a debt, a door you'd walked through, and a voice that said: I'll find you.

Every girl was her. You know it the way you know your own name. The hair, the eyes, the smoke, the warm bronze skin, the laugh that keeps getting away from her. Every time you got close she slipped out of your hands.

Her lips hover an inch from yours, patient and sure. It is the name you've been missing all along, and it is right there, heavy as a stone in your mouth. You say it, quietly, against her lips. "{goddess}."

teases.title: New rules

image.comp: a girl straddling a man on a bed, hands on his chest, a wicked smile, looking down at him

teases.text:
{goddess} arrives as {alias} tonight, {form}, hands on her hips, with the air of someone about to read terms and conditions.

"So you know. Which is a nuisance, because the disguises are fun and I'm not giving them up." She walks around you in a slow circle. "New rules. I come as someone new. You can play along, or you can call me by my name and I'll punish you. Either way, you don't finish. That part doesn't change."

"Is that a rule or a punishment?"

"Yes."

choices.label: Play along
choices.res: "Good," says {alias}, with a slow, wicked smile, settling into your lap as if she'd been introduced for the first time. The game is terrible, and wonderful.
choices.resIn: You play along, and she brightens like a lamp being lit. "Good," says {alias}. "Then let's begin. Hello, stranger." She slides into your lap.

choices.label: "Nice to meet you, {goddess}."
choices.res: "Oh, you're going to pay for that." She pushes you back onto the bed and makes you, thoroughly, until you're begging. She never gives you what you're begging for.
choices.resIn: "Nice to meet you, {goddess}," you say politely, and watch her eyes narrow with a wicked light. "Oh, you will pay for that," she promises, and takes hold of your tie.

teases.intro:
The office is dim, and you're expecting trouble. You've been expecting it since the roof; every footfall in the hall is a possible goddess. When the door opens, you don't even look up.

"Good evening." {alias}, {form}, standing with her hands on her hips, hair swinging to her knees, gold tips glowing, eyes bright with mischief. She has the air of someone about to read out terms and conditions. {goddess} has dressed for the occasion in someone else's face.

"So you know," she says, walking a slow circle around your chair. "Which is a nuisance, because I like the disguises and I'm not giving them up."
teases.wonder:
She's enjoying this enormously. You can tell, because she can't quite keep her mouth straight, and because she keeps rolling the new name around in her mouth as though it were a sweet.

You know exactly who is under the ears. Knowing changes things. It means that when she looks at you like that, there is a person behind the look, someone who has been waiting an awfully long time. It also means that you're in a great deal of trouble.

"New rules," she announces, and perches on the edge of the desk. "I come as someone new. You can play along, or you can call me by my real name, and I'll punish you. Either way, you don't finish. That part doesn't change." You raise an eyebrow. "Is that a rule or a punishment?"

"Yes."

teases.title: Introductions
teases.text:
{alias}, {form}, knocks on the office door and waits to be asked in, an act which is not at all like her.

"Good evening. I'm new in town." She holds out a hand, perfectly innocent. "I heard the owner could use some help." Her eyes are glowing gold and entirely innocent. Her hand is already inside your coat.

"You haven't introduced yourself," you say, and she gives you a look that says play along or suffer.

choices.label: "Welcome. What can you do?"
choices.res: "Oh," says the stranger, "a great many things." She shows you a few. All of them. None to completion. You're going to be walking funny for a while.
choices.resIn: "Oh," says the stranger, brightening, "a great many things." She closes the office door with her heel and does not look at all innocent.

choices.label: "{goddess}, you're a terrible actress."
choices.res: "I'm a wonderful actress and you are a spoilsport." She taps your nose, scandalized. "I'll have to teach you manners." By the end of the night, you're the one who has learned a lesson.
choices.resIn: "I'm a wonderful actress and you are a spoilsport," says the stranger, offended, and shows you exactly how she means to make it up to you.

teases.intro:
{alias}, {form}, knocks on the office door and waits to be asked in, an act which is not at all like her. Having been at the ledgers for hours, you look up with your pen halfway through a sum.

"Good evening." She comes in with small, careful steps, hands clasped, eyes cast down. Long black hair, gold-tipped, drifting around her like smoke. "I'm new in town. I heard the owner could use some help."

She offers you a hand, perfectly innocent. You take it. Her other hand, you note, is already inside your coat.
teases.wonder:
This is the part you used to dread: the strange woman, the warm smile, the sinking feeling that you'd been caught in a trap. Now you know exactly whose trap it is. You know the shape of the eyes under the lowered lashes. You know the laugh she's swallowing.

It's ridiculous, and it's oddly sweet. She has been a stranger so many times that she has turned it into an art form, and tonight, she's decided to let you see the seams.

You wonder how long she can keep it up, and how far she'll go before the mask cracks. Whether, this time, she might let you finish. She looks up at you with huge, solemn gold eyes, wholly innocent. "You haven't introduced yourself, sir," says the stranger.

teases.title: Wrong pretext

image.comp: a girl wearing glasses and carrying a stack of books, leaning over a man seated at a desk, her hand on his shoulder, playful smile

teases.text:
The knock on the door is very polite. {alias} is standing outside in {form}, carrying a stack of books, wearing a pair of spectacles she definitely doesn't need.

"Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson." She's trying very hard not to laugh. "I understand it's... hands-on."

She is not subtle. You do not mind. Forty minutes of 'lessons' later, you've learned that a goddess in spectacles is considerably more dangerous than one without, and that she has no intention of giving you the final exam.

choices.label: Insist on a retake
choices.res: "No retakes," she says, smugly, tying her hair back. "Fail, learn, repeat." She kisses your forehead on the way out, which is somehow the worst part.
choices.resIn: "A retake? Already?" She sets down the book, eyes dancing. "Very well. Let's see what you remember."

choices.label: Beg for extra credit
choices.res: "Begging. Good start." She's glowing with satisfaction. She doesn't award extra credit.
choices.resIn: "Extra credit?" She taps her chin as if it's a serious question. "That depends. How badly do you want it?"

teases.intro:
The knock on the door is very polite. You've been waiting for it, in a way; there was a note on your desk this morning in handwriting you didn't recognise, saying only: "Lessons, seven o'clock." You've been trying not to wonder.

{alias} is standing outside in {form}, with a stack of books clutched to her chest and a pair of spectacles on her nose that she definitely doesn't need. Her hair is bound in a single tidy braid, and the gold tip swings as she nods. "Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson." She's trying very hard not to laugh. "I understand it's... hands-on."
teases.wonder:
You know who she is. You know, and she knows you know, and you're both going to pretend very seriously that neither of you does. Somewhere in the back of your mind, a very small voice points out that this is absurd.

The spectacles slide down her nose, and she pushes them back with one finger, solemn as a clerk. A goddess of unknown age, in a pair of borrowed glasses, trying to look as if she's never seen a man before. It is probably the most ridiculous thing you've ever witnessed, and you can't stop smiling.

She opens a book at random and holds it up between you. "I'll start with a review," says {alias}, peeking over the top. "Unless you'd rather skip to the practical?"

teases.title: A new face, an old game
teases.text: Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across your desk and pretending very hard that you haven't met. "I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she says, as her foot slides up the inside of your thigh. You play along. She's very good. She's also absolutely merciless, and leaves you exactly one breath from the edge.

choices.label: Call her by name
choices.res: "{goddess}." Her mask slips, just a little, and she's smiling so wide you can feel it. "Good boy." She kisses you, and doesn't let you finish.
choices.resIn: "{goddess}," you say, mildly. Her toes stop, and her grin breaks wide. "Spoilsport," she murmurs, delighted, and slides off the desk into your lap.

choices.label: Stay in character
choices.res: "Until next time," she says. "Remember my name." She leaves it unsaid, which is part of the game.
choices.resIn: "We've never met," you agree solemnly. She makes a pleased little noise, and the foot travels higher.

teases.intro:
Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across your desk and pretending very hard that you haven't met. She has pushed the ledger aside to make room, black hair spilling over the pages in a shining river, the gold tips lighting the blotted figures from below. Her eyes are bright, and dancing, and perfectly innocent.

"I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she says, with a perfectly straight face, as a bare foot slides slowly along the arm of your chair. "Have we done business before?"
teases.wonder:
You play along, because it's easier than arguing and because you're curious how long she can hold the straight face. Not long, from the look of it: the corner of her mouth keeps betraying her. Every time you almost laugh, she nudges you with a toe.

You wonder whether tonight is the night she'll let you finish. You doubt it. Her toes are very warm and entirely too confident, and the look in her eyes says she has a plan. You just have to decide whether to give her the satisfaction of her name.

teases.title: Pick a name
teases.text:
{alias}, {form}, is waiting in the hall. "Guess," she says, and wraps herself around you. "Go on. I'll give you a point for every correct answer." You guess 'Seliora' on the first try. She gives you a point. The point is one very pointed kiss.

The game goes on a good deal longer than you'd like. It ends the usual way.

choices.label: Call her by name
choices.res: "{goddess}." Her mask slips, just a little, and she's smiling so wide you can feel it. "Good boy." She kisses you, and doesn't let you finish.
choices.resIn: "{goddess}," you say, on the first try. "A point," she says, thrilled, and her answer is a very pointed kiss.

choices.label: Stay in character
choices.res: She leaves laughing, a little breathless, a little pleased with herself.
choices.resIn: You pretend to think hard, and she pretends to be impatient, and the two of you very nearly manage to keep a straight face.

teases.intro:
{alias}, {form}, is waiting in the upstairs hall, leaning against the wall under a lantern as though she owned the house, which, strictly, she might. Her black hair falls past her knees, gold at the ends like a candle snuffed mid-burn. When you come round the corner she steps into your path, smiling, and drapes herself around you without any warning at all.

"Guess," she says, her lips at your ear. "Go on. I'll give you a point for every correct answer."
teases.wonder:
You know that she wants you to say the name. You also know that saying it will cost you something, and not saying it will cost you something else. It's a nice sort of problem, you decide, the kind that smells of candle smoke and warm skin.

She's pressed close enough that you can feel her laugh before you hear it, and her hands have started to wander as if looking for the answer on you. Whatever you pick, she is going to enjoy it a great deal.

teases.title: Playing a part
teases.text: Tonight {alias} is {form}, shy and sweet and clumsy, tripping into your arms and not apologizing. "Oh, I'm so sorry," she says, in a voice that has never been sorry in its life, and the way her hands wander is not at all clumsy. It ends the way it always does, and you're very nearly proud of how much you're able to take.

"Oh, I'm so sorry," she says, wide-eyed, in a voice that has never been sorry in its life.

She isn't sorry. She isn't clumsy, either, and the hands pressed flat to your chest are far too sure of themselves. You're nearly proud of how well you're holding up; it's quite a performance, and you've seen her do worse.

She peeks up at you through her lashes, a picture of bashful innocence, and you feel the whole act wind itself up like a spring. Somewhere beneath the blush, a goddess is trying very hard not to laugh.

teases.title: Herself

image.comp: a tall goddess with glowing skin sitting on the edge of a man's bed at night, hair loose, leaning in for a slow kiss, candle-light and a floating ember-flame

teases.text:
For the first time in a very long time, {goddess} comes to you as herself. No ears, no tail, no wings: just a tall, bronze, glowing woman with eyes the color of lamp-flame, sitting on the edge of your bed with her hair loose over her shoulders.

"I got tired of being someone else," she says. "For tonight, at least." She leans down and kisses you, slow, and you feel the tremor in her. "Tell me what you remember."

{goddess} is waiting in your room with her arms folded, every candle burning an offended, sulky orange.

"{n}. {n} of them." She doesn't say of what. "Tonight you're mine. Don't argue, I'm a goddess."

She pulls you down onto the bed and keeps you there all night: close, closer, never all the way, her hands and mouth making very sure you won't forget whose bed this is. She never once lets you finish.

choices.label: "You could just stay."
choices.res: She goes very still. "No," she says. "I couldn't." Then, quieter, into your shoulder: "It wasn't a whim, you know. Forget I said that." She stays until dawn anyway.

This time she doesn't stop at the edge. She takes you in, slow, eyes closed, gold markings blazing along her hips, and for a moment the whole room is lantern-light, every flame bowing toward you both.

Then her hand is flat on your chest. "Stop. Stay. Don't." Her voice isn't steady. "If you finish in me I'm yours. Not as a figure of speech. And I've wanted you for far longer than you know." She stays exactly like that, holding you both on the edge, until she can let go of you without either of you breaking.

choices.res: You do. It is the hardest thing you've ever done. Afterwards she lies on your chest for a long time and doesn't disappear.

choices.label: "Would that be so bad?"

teases.text:
{goddess} visits more often now and leaves later. She takes you all the way in and stops, every time, at the very last moment, with a sound like it costs her more than it costs you.

"You know what I'd lose." Her forehead against yours. "Everything I am. And I'd be yours. I watched you for years before the truck, you know. Years. I don't even know which of those scares me more."

choices.label: "I'd give it back."

{goddess} sits on the windowsill, glowing faintly, the ember-flame dozing against her neck, looking at the house.

"One of them has done it all now, you know. Lived and lived again, as far as a life can carry." She doesn't look at you. "You fed that stray cat every morning for two years and nobody ever saw. I saw. It wasn't a whim, {sam}. It never was." She finally turns. "When you bring her back next time, I'm coming too. I don't think I can watch from the lanterns anymore."

choices.label: "Then come."
choices.res: "Next time," she says. "Finish what you started." Then she's gone, and the window is only a window.

choices.label: "You're sure?"
choices.res: "No." She smiles, crooked. "Goddesses are never sure. We just act like it."

Every lantern in {house} flickers at once. Someone giggles. Nobody else hears it.
You find a single small ember on your pillow, still warm, burning nothing. Under it, in a very elegant hand: "Busy week? I enjoyed the show."

{goddess} appears in your room the night after you were with someone else. She doesn't say anything. She just sits there glowing at you, pointedly, her dress sliding lower by the minute, until you apologize for something you can't name.
"{lady} again?" The voice is at your ear, warm and dry, and a hand you can't see settles at your belt. "I'll remember that. I'll want to compare."

{goddess} catches you in the hallway, pins you to the wall by the collar and kisses you hard enough to hurt, hands already inside your shirt. "So you remember who was first," she says, and is gone.
"How many, {sam}?" She isn't smiling. Her hand is on your chest, warm and possessive. "How many before you look up?"

remarkChoices.label: Reassure her
remarkChoices.res: "You were first. You'll always be first." A long pause. "...Fine," says the dark, mollified.

remarkChoices.label: Let it go
remarkChoices.res: You let it go. Somewhere, a goddess sulks.

binding.title: Bound

binding.text:
This time the lanterns don't wait for you to wake. {goddess} is there before the dark is finished, and she doesn't say "again."

"{names} has lived it all now. Everything a life can carry. And so have I, watching you." She pulls you down with her. "I told you it was a whim. It wasn't. Years, {sam}. Years of watching you be kind when nobody was looking: the stray cat you fed every single morning for two years, all the little things nobody ever thanked you for. I wanted you the whole time. I'm done watching."

She doesn't stop you this time. She holds on, and when you finish inside her the light goes out of her like a breath let go: the glow under her skin, the gold markings, the little ember-flame, the warmth that never came from anywhere. Every lantern goes dark at once.

What's left is a woman with gold eyes, shaking, laughing, holding on to you.
binding.after:
"Oh," she says. "Oh, that's cold. Is it always this cold?" She burrows into you. "I'm yours now. All of me, the little that's left. I wanted you since before the truck, and I'd never have said so with the light still on. You'll have to build me back up, {sam}."
